clue.text: Easy to read stage dropping first bit of bible

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: dropping the first bit means the opening letter of the word bible is lost

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone finds a play script readable once its biblical opening is skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' could be a theatre platform, but here it is a leg of a journey; 'dropping first bit of' acts on the word bible itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Legible writing is clear enough that it can be read without effort.

clue.text: Rock with body odour at monastic basin

parts.note: lava is molten rock, which sets into rock

explanation.surface: A smelly stone sits by the washbasin in a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A lavabo is the basin monks or priests use for ritual washing of the hands.

clue.text: It requires pluck to play this

definitions.text: It requires pluck to play this

parts.words: It requires pluck to play this
parts.note: pluck seems to mean courage, as if some game or role needs nerve; here it is literal plucking of strings on an instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A stringed instrument is played by plucking or strumming its strings.

clue.text: Boycott god of thunder at point of fruit tree

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, as a union might black goods
Thor is the Norse god of thunder
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A protest against the thunder god takes place by an orchard tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The sloe bush bears small sour fruit and is a thorny shrub or small tree.

clue.text: Superfluous that former skill returned

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: returned means the word for skill is read backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a talent once possessed came back but was no longer needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' acts on the word for skill alone; 'former' is the usual crossword signal for the prefix meaning ex-.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional beyond what is needed is surplus to requirements.

clue.text: Sweet desert animal with a leading role

indicators.note: with here means the animal holds the other letters, carrying them inside it

parts.note: a camel is the classic animal of the desert

indicators.note: leading means only the first letter of role is taken

explanation.surface: A dromedary is given the starring part in a confectionery advert.
explanation.walkthrough: A and R (the start of 'role') go inside CAMEL after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is a toffee-like confection made from heated sugar.

clue.text: Inoculant used with perpetual regularity

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the adjective sense of recurring again and again

indicators.note: used suggests the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A vaccine is administered over and over without a break.
explanation.definitionFit: Continual describes something recurring frequently and repeatedly over time.

clue.text: Knocks up a fight

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for fight is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice

explanation.surface: A brawl gets someone knocked up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SPAR, reading it backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Raps are sharp blows, such as taps on a door.

clue.text: Sad odes doctor takes on and perishes

indicators.note: takes means the doctor's letters hold the next word inside them

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a military doctor
taken as written
dies means perishes

explanation.surface: A medic composing mournful poems carries on, then passes away.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, a military medical officer, is a common crossword abbreviation for doctor; 'takes' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A monody is a mournful poem or lament sung by one voice.

clue.text: Gift to recognise great ship back home

clue.text: There you are viola playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with, set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A musician hands over a stringed instrument mid-performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Voila is a French-derived exclamation used when presenting something completed.

clue.text: Can first batsman recognise kitchen appliance

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Can first batsman recognise kitchen appliance (3,6)': TIN + OPENER fits, but 'recognise' has no job in any parse; the clue looks corrupted ('recognise' also intrudes in 8-down).
annotationWithheld.clue: Can first batsman recognise kitchen appliance

clue.text: One's not a very good passenger in this

definitions.text: One's not a very good passenger in this

parts.words: One's not a very good passenger in this
parts.note: seems to describe a poor travelling companion; really someone not very good, a criminal, is carried as a passenger in a police vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: This is old slang for the police van used to carry arrested prisoners.

clue.text: Paid father out a pound, a point of doing nothing

indicators.note: out means the letters for father leave the word Paid

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A dad was paid off with a pound for sitting around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid' is fodder here, not a verb; 'out' signals the deletion, and compass points are a standard source of single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being idle is being inactive or unoccupied.

clue.text: Seeing what's said of the pig Ireland made

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are made into something new, shaped afresh

explanation.surface: An Irish pig is seen being turned into something.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading is understanding speech by watching the movements of a speaker's mouth.

clue.text: Display concern for entertainment industry

parts.note: a show is a display
a concern is a business, a company

explanation.surface: A firm shows interest in the world of entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the professional world of theatre, film, television and popular music.

clue.text: Very little point remains following harmless fibs

parts.note: a whit is a very small amount, as in not a whit
E, east, is a point of the compass
lies means remains, stays in place

explanation.surface: A tiny pointless detail stays behind to excuse small untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small untruths told to be tactful or polite rather than to deceive harmfully.

clue.text: Wrestlers hold the shears

definitions.meaning: a wrestling grip with the legs locked round an opponent
a cutting tool with two crossed blades

explanation.surface: Grappling athletes grasp a pair of clippers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are named for the crossing action: a leg grip in wrestling and the bladed cutting tool.

clue.text: Rise firm to start or represent

parts.note: to stand is to rise to one's feet

indicators.note: to start means only the opening letter of firm is used

explanation.surface: Someone must get up early to act on behalf of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes F, the first letter of 'firm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Initials or symbols stand for things when they signify or mean them.

clue.text: Gives food with support for larvae

indicators.note: with means the word for food-giving holds the support within it

parts.note: caters means provides food
a pillar is a support, a column

explanation.surface: A caterer provides meals with a column supporting the tent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is an unusual container signal: the food-giving word holds the support among its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the grub stage of butterflies and moths, before they pupate.

clue.text: Erica takes in jacket padding

indicators.note: takes means the word for heather holds the next word inside it

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heathers, and ling is heather
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman named Erica takes the padding out of a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name but is the heather genus; 'takes' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Lining is the inner layer of material sewn into a garment.

clue.text: Agreed it comes between a French credit centre

indicators.note: comes between means the word it is placed after the French word and before the next piece

parts.note: un is French for a
taken as written

indicators.note: centre means the middle letters of credit are taken

explanation.surface: An agreement places something between a French loan and its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' picks the middle two letters of an even-length word; 'comes between' sets the order of the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined together in agreement or common purpose.

clue.text: Go down with immoral act at kings head

parts.note: a sin is an immoral act

indicators.note: head means the first letter of kings is used

explanation.surface: A ruler descends into wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to drop down or descend, especially below water.

clue.text: Primates turn up for allowance detachment

indicators.note: turn up means the word for primates is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: apes are primates
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Monkeys arrive to collect their share and then stay apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' could mean arrive; here it signals the reversal of the primates.
explanation.definitionFit: A separation is a parting or the state of being apart.

clue.text: Some inclination to fish

definitions.meaning: a slope or tilt, the measure of how much something leans
to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: An urge to go fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a slant or degree of lean; the other is to catch fish with hook and line.

clue.text: A dispute about young shellfish

definitions.meaning: the spawn or young of oysters and similar molluscs

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over baby oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a minor quarrel; the other is the larval spawn of bivalves such as oysters.

clue.text: A bit aloof well may be the issue

parts.note: off means rather cool and unfriendly, slightly distant in manner
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: A slightly distant well might be the cause of the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a problem but means children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a legal term for children or descendants.

clue.text: Amin turns to being the moron again

parts.note: Idi Amin was the Ugandan dictator

indicators.note: turns means the little word to is turned around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The dictator Amin again reveals himself a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Idi Amin, the 1970s Ugandan dictator, gives his first name; 'turns' signals the reversal of the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are insulting terms for a very stupid person.

clue.text: Fairies persist in dancing

indicators.note: dancing suggests the letters are moving about into new positions

explanation.surface: Little magical folk keep on dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites are elves or small supernatural beings of folklore.

clue.text: Sign of busy toilet before the match

definitions.meaning: the word shown on a lavatory door lock when it is occupied

explanation.surface: A sign shows the loo is occupied before kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the match' suggests a sporting fixture but means a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is occupied, as a lavatory; the other is betrothed to be married.
